evidence.documentation: Not affected. The PR body marks documentation as unchanged, and the change is a behavior bug fix in internal CSS, not a new feature or documented behavior change.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The fix changes visible GUI behavior on mobile under a user-accessible setting (prefers-reduced-motion). No human is known to have exercised this path. The existing Playwright test drives the same interaction model a user would, but the merge-group workflow failure noted above means CI coverage is not fully reliable for this change.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after the first (and only) approval. The PR contains one content commit (63cdcf6) and one merge commit (8542787). The branch was updated via a rebase-merge of main at 2026-10-27T02:22:41Z, which preceded the approval.

The reviewer has subject-matter expertise (GUI, app, a11y) per docs/dev/contribute.md. It verifies: (1) the sheet has `aria-hidden='true'` initially and is positioned below the viewport edge, (2) the composer is focusable and receives focus, (3) opening the sheet via the mobile menu button works, (4) drag-to-dismiss moves the sheet down and restores `aria-hidden`, and (5) the Close button dismisses and refocuses the composer. The original pre-approval statusCheckRollup shows the related 'App docs, typecheck, runtime and UI tests' check passed (SUCCESS). However, the merge-group run of the 'Lemonade App checks' workflow concluded FAILURE. The PR was merged anyway, suggesting the failure was transient or bypassed. No evidence of human manual testing on a real device exists.

maintainer_todos.text: Enable prefers-reduced-motion on a mobile-size viewport (390×844), confirm the closed Conversations sheet sits below the visible area and does not cover the composer, then tap the composer to verify focus returns.

Open the Conversations sheet, drag the handle downward, and confirm the sheet dismisses and the composer regains focus; repeat using the Close button on the sheet to verify both dismissal paths work under reduced motion.

subject: fix(gui3): keep mobile conversation sheet hidden with reduced motion (#3962)
summary: Removes the conflicting `transform: none !important` override from the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` CSS block in both `styles.css` and `critical.generated.css`, so the mobile Conversations bottom sheet slides off-screen when closed instead of remaining visible and covering the chat composer; extends Playwright A11y test A34 at 390×844 to verify closed position, drag-to-dismiss, close-button dismissal, and composer focus return.
verdict_reason: This is a small, focused CSS fix with an approved reviewer who has GUI/a11y expertise and no post-approval churn, but it changes mobile GUI behavior under a specific accessibility setting without evidence of manual verification, and the merge-group run of the Lemonade App checks workflow failed before merge.
